subject: Post-call: RetailCo model evals + quality regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@retailco.com>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@retailco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended models / next steps

Hi Alex / Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: improve recommendations relevancy on product search and upsell prompts while keeping latency under 350ms P95 for your peak storefront load.
- Current setup: you’re evaluating open models on our Dedicated cluster; last week an internal test switched to small-LM-v3 (quantized) and you saw mixed results.

Redwood recommendation (short list)\- small-LM-quantized-v3.0 — best cost/latency tradeoff in our benchmarks for retail conversational prompts\- base-LM-1.1 (higher-quality) — recommended for critical upsell flows where precision matters

Attachments: I’ve attached our evaluation summary (retailco_eval_v2.pdf) and the prompt set we used (prompt_set_user_queries_v1.csv). The Drive folder has the full benchmark runs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RetailCoBench

Next steps
1) You to confirm which flows you want us to run the 2k-sample evaluation on (search vs upsell vs cart prompts).
2) If helpful, we can pin a model/version on your Dedicated pool (no infra changes) for a short A/B.
3) Follow-up 30-min call next week to review diffs and agree on rollout. 

If you’d like I can loop in Dev (solutions) and Dylan (CS) for the A/B plan.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: retailco_eval_v2.pdf (18 pages), prompt_set_user_queries_v1.csv (2,000 rows)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@retailco.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended models / next steps

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa. Helpful. A quick update from our side before we schedule the follow-up: 

We ran a smoke pass overnight against the search flow using your prompt set. Unfortunately we started seeing a reproducible quality regression compared to the v2 baseline after our infra team allowed an automatic update from small-LM-v3.0 -> small-LM-v3.1 on Wed morning. Typical examples attached (examples_regression.txt).

Symptoms:
- Higher hallucination rate on product attribute answers (~8% -> ~17% on a 500-sample test)
- Shorter responses that drop required qualifiers (e.g., "in stock" -> "sometimes")

Can you confirm whether v3.1 includes any decoding/config defaults changes or model deltas? If this is a model-side regression we need options for pinning/rollback ASAP — the recommender touches live search.

Sam, looping you (ops) and Procurement for context if we need a change order or support SLA.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Sr. Product Manager, Retail Search | RetailCo
alex.rivera@retailco.com

Dev / Dylan — forwarding Alex's note. RetailCo observed a regression after an automatic update from small-LM-v3.0 -> v3.1 on their Dedicated pool. Key asks from Alex: 
- Confirm what changed between v3.0 and v3.1 (model diffs or config defaults)
- Recommend immediate mitigation (pin, rollback) and estimated time to restore
- Summary we can share with Procurement if needed

Attachments sent by Alex: examples_regression.txt (5 examples). I’ve also attached the eval summary and our prompt set to help triage.

Recommended immediate action: if we can pin their pool to v3.0 while we triage that would be safest — Alex flagged this as impacting search. Let me know if that is doable and timeline.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: retailco_eval_v2.pdf, prompt_set_user_queries_v1.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@retailco.com>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@retailco.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + recommended models / quality regression observed by RetailCo

Hi team — thanks for the examples, Alex. Quick triage notes and proposed plan below.

Findings (preliminary)
- Small-LM-v3.1 includes a minor tokenizer normalization change and a default top_p adjustment (0.95 -> 0.9) we rolled out to reduce tail token cost. That decode default can increase truncation/hallucination on certain retail prompts.
- No architecture change; weights are backward compatible, but the decoding default is likely the root cause here.

Immediate mitigation (what I can do right now)
1) Pin RetailCo's Dedicated pool to small-LM-v3.0 (no infra downtime). I can apply this within 2 hours after approval.
2) Produce a one-page model_diff_summary.txt explaining the tokenizer/decode deltas and the expected impact. (attached)
3) Run a quick 500-sample rerun on your prompt set against v3.0 vs v3.1 and share delta metrics (I’ll push results to the Drive folder). Estimated 6 hours.

Longer-term options
- We can back out the top_p default change for your pool and run targeted evals to see if that resolves the hallucination without pinning.
- If you prefer, we can keep v3.1 but adjust decode params at the route level to match v3.0 behavior.

Please confirm if you want me to proceed with pinning to v3.0 now. If Procurement needs a formal change order for pinned version support, loop them and we’ll produce a short SOW.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0133

Attachments: model_diff_summary.txt (1 page)
